subject.title: fix(plugins): surface oversized-file warnings in doctor migration reads

question: Should doctor continue to migrate legacy Active Memory, Device Pair, and Reef state above 10 MiB through a safe bounded path, or is warning-and-skip an approved upgrade contract with an explicit recovery flow?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes how already persisted user state is handled during migration; choosing between complete bounded migration and an operator recovery contract is product and upgrade-policy judgment, not a mechanical code choice.

options.title: Preserve supported migration
options.body: Implement descriptor-safe bounded migration or a format-specific safe strategy so valid existing legacy state remains migratable without silently stranding it.

options.title: Approve explicit recovery
options.body: Keep the cap only with a maintainer-approved doctor-visible recovery workflow that tells affected users how to preserve and import the legacy values.

recommendation.title: Preserve supported migration
recommendation.body: Implement descriptor-safe bounded migration or a format-specific safe strategy so valid existing legacy state remains migratable without silently stranding it.

likelyOwner.reason: The final implementation commit and regression tests establish the current warning-and-skip behavior, making this the closest evidence-backed routing contact.
